22 A vehicle is moving with a speed of 30.0 m s–1 directly towards a stationary observer. The horn of
the vehicle emits sound of frequency 440 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s–1.
What is the frequency of the sound heard by the observer?
A
401 Hz
B
404 Hz
C
479 Hz
D
483 Hz

hints: Notice the $30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ vehicle is moving directly towards the stationary observer, so successive $440 \text{ Hz}$ wavefronts are crowded together.
For sound with speed $340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, the observed wavelength is shortened to $(v - v_s)/f_s$ when the source approaches, so observed frequency must be greater than $440 \text{ Hz}$.
Calculate $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$ with $f_s = 440 \text{ Hz}$, $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and check which option near $480 \text{ Hz}$ matches.
walkthrough: Identify the situation: source speed $v_s = 30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a stationary observer, source frequency $f_s = 440 \text{ Hz}$, wave speed $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall the Doppler rule for a moving source: motion towards the observer shortens the observed wavelength, so $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$ and $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$.
Substitute the values with units: $f_o = 440 \text{ Hz} \times 340/(340 - 30.0)$ where speeds are in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Evaluate the denominator: $340 - 30.0 = 310 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $f_o = 440 \times 340/310 \text{ Hz}$.
Calculate the intermediate ratio: $340/310 \approx 1.097$, so $f_o \approx 440 \times 1.097 \approx 483 \text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$.
Check sense: the frequency is higher than $440 \text{ Hz}$, as expected for approach, and matches the larger value offered. This is option D.

A.explanation: Gives $440 \times (340-30)/340$. This inverts the Doppler fraction and gives a lower frequency for a source moving towards the observer.

B.explanation: Gives $440 \times 340/(340+30)$. Adding the $30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ source speed increases the observed wavelength, which is for a receding source, not an approaching one.

C.explanation: Close to the correct value but too low. Using the correct denominator $340-30 = 310 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives about $483 \text{ Hz}$, not $479 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: Uses $440 \times 340/(340-30)$ for an approaching source, giving about $483 \text{ Hz}$, which is higher than $440 \text{ Hz}$ as expected.
